content.text:
I've submitted index 10 (Ca 0.314 / Mn 0.686) as the best composition. At 1.88 µA it had the highest photocurrent of the three I measured, which used up the whole merit budget. I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements.

| Index | Ca fraction | Nearby phase | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|---|
| 23 | 0.398 | Ca2Mn3O8 (predicted gap 2.69 eV) | 0.39 µA |
| 8 | 0.338 | CaMn2O4 (predicted gap 2.54 eV) | 1.74 µA |
| 10 | 0.314 | Just Mn-rich of CaMn2O4 | 1.88 µA |

- **Why this region:** CaMn2O4 has a predicted band gap of 2.54 eV, so it can absorb the 3.22 eV light. The stability model puts it on the convex hull, meaning it should be stable.
- **Why I stopped at 0.314:** photocurrent kept rising as the Mn fraction went up. But the phases expected further toward Mn have much smaller predicted gaps (0.3–0.9 eV), so I didn't push further on the last measurement.
- **What's untested:** the very Mn-rich end (Ca below 0.25) and the Ca-rich end (Ca 0.5 and above) weren't measured. The main phases expected at the Ca-rich end have predicted gaps under 0.3 eV. The rising trend means a better composition slightly more Mn-rich than index 10 can't be ruled out. The Gaussian-process model's top suggestion was index 19 (Ca 0.245), but I didn't measure it.
